test: Compute late dollar-days per paid invoice = amount x max(0, pay_day - due_day) from finance_invoices joined to finance_customer_payments; aggregate by customer, rank, and measure the share held by top 10%/20% of customers vs their share of billed dollars. Break down by terms_days, credit_limit band, branch, year, and check whether days-late per customer is dispersed beyond what dollar volume explains (compare concentration of late dollar-days to concentration of billed dollars). Size: average late balance x 8% cost of capital, and the part attributable to the concentrated customers above baseline.
support: Top decile of customers holds a clearly larger share of late dollar-days than of billed dollars; mean days-late differs materially by customer or terms; persistent per-customer lateness year to year.
weaken: Late dollar-day concentration mirrors revenue concentration (same top-decile share); days-late distribution per customer is narrow and identical across terms/credit bands; no year-to-year persistence, consistent with a generated schedule.
expect: I expect the hypothesis mostly to fail in its behavioural form: late dollar-days will be concentrated only because revenue is concentrated, and per-customer lateness will look uniform (generated payments). Moderate confidence (~65%) it does not hold beyond revenue concentration.
